name: 10 x 24 manual surface grinder
about: Links from the GrabCAD STEP (moonshot/library/stations/extract.py; bounds, volumes and inertias in sgrind.links.json), in a world frame with the floor at z = 0, the table's middle at x = 0, the wheel's mid-plane at y = 0 and the operator at -Y. Joint zero is the STEP's pose: the table centred, the 10 in wheel 163.1 mm above the chuck, the chuck lever pointing right (off). The STEP has no maker, so its working numbers come from makers' manuals and listings for manual grinders: South Bend's SB1029 6 x 18 manual (hand-feed, the controls and the order of work), Clausing's CSG2A1020 10 x 20 (travel) and Suburban's 10 x 24 fine-pole permanent chuck. Sources: cad is measured on the STEP, naming its solids by their index in the file; spec is a maker's figure for this machine's class, named in each reason; proposed has its reason.

sources.sb1029: South Bend Lathe Co., Model SB1029 6 x 18 Surface Grinder Owner's Manual (2010), https://archive.org/download/manualsonline-id-7918a92e-d1b2-4fbe-bb4c-6217a681a58e/7918a92e-d1b2-4fbe-bb4c-6217a681a58e.pdf: Machine Specifications (p. 4-5), Additional Surface Grinder Safety (p. 8), Test Run (p. 19), Operation Overview and Controls (p. 20-21), Wheel Dressing (p. 28), Magnetic Chuck, Setup and Using the Surface Grinder (p. 31-32)
sources.clausing: Clausing Industrial, CSG2A1020 Manual Precision Surface Grinder, 10 x 20 in, https://clausing-industrial.com/product/csg2a1020/
sources.suburban: Suburban Tool fine-pole permanent magnetic chucks (1/8 in poles, 1/8 in separators, ceramic): MCB-1024-FP 24-1/2 x 10 x 2-5/8 in, https://exacttooling.com/products/08542391; MCB-824-FP 126 lb, https://penntoolco.com/suburban-tool-rectangular-permanent-magnetic-chuck-mcb-824-fp-fine-pole-24-1-2-x-8-x-2-5-8-77-552-8
sources.mcmaster_chucks: McMaster-Carr, magnetic workholding chucks: permanent-magnet chucks hold up to 30 psi, rare-earth 115 psi; fine pole spacing for parts smaller or thinner than 1/4 in, https://www.mcmaster.com/products/magnetic-workholding-chucks
sources.sharp: Sharp SG-618 6 x 18 manual surface grinder, dealer listing of the maker's specification: longitudinal hand feed 2.7 in per turn, https://blumberg.machinehub.com/listing/new-6-x-18-sharp-sg-618-manual-surface-grinder-3/
sources.osha: OSHA 29 CFR 1910.215(b)(4): on surface grinders the guard's exposure angle may not exceed 150 deg, beginning not more than 15 deg above the horizontal plane of the spindle, https://www.osha.gov/laws-regs/regulations/standardnumber/1910/1910.215
sources.tormach: Tormach PSG 612 Operator's Manual UM10159, https://tormach.com/docs/download/assetlink/asset_id/431: Using the Magnetic Chuck (a wrench on its front face turned to on or off, p. 12), Dressing a Wheel (the dresser on the chuck, p. 16)
sources.butler_1a1r: Butler Bros, 6 x 0.035 x 1-1/4 in diamond wheel, resin bond, type 1A1R, 120 grit (ASD120-R100B99-1/4: 1/4 in diamond depth, 6,048 rpm max), https://shop.butlerbros.com/catalogue/product/1042056

gaps: Cross travel is what the STEP's column allows: 140 mm toward it before the table's back edge reaches the column's face (150 mm), 75 mm toward the operator. The wheel then reaches the chuck's back 202 mm of its 254 mm width, not all of it as on a real 10 x 24 grinder (Clausing's 10 x 20 crosses 11.81 in). A part set within that reach grinds as on the real machine

The table stops (solids 51, 52) and the centre stop (48-50) are drawn where the STEP has them (one already 5 mm into the centre stop) and stop nothing: the table's travel is its joint's range, and a hand reverses the traverse

The STEP draws the chuck's top with 24 strips 1/4 in wide at 3/4 in pitch; its hold is Suburban's fine-pole chuck's (1/8 in poles), as the chuck a 1/8 in insert needs. The strips are drawn as they are
The STEP has no spindle motor: its mass (about 30 kg for 2 hp) isn't added to the wheelhead. It changes only the down-feed handwheel's effort, by 0.6 N at the rim
A permanent chuck's residual magnetism in the part after it is switched off is not modelled

The STEP has no control box and no coolant: the box here (the controls link, on a bracket off the base's right side) is made in extract.py with SB1029's ON and OFF buttons, power light and coolant switch, and the coolant's nozzle on the guard (coolant)
A part resting on a held part (on a parallel, say) isn't pulled through it: the flux a steel parallel carries up into what stands on it is not modelled

density_source.reason: The saddle's and the table's solids are filled where their castings are ribbed: cast iron's 7.2 halved, about the share of a ribbed casting that is iron (the table 118 kg, the saddle 268 kg). The chuck weighs Suburban's figure: the MCB-824-FP's 126 lb scaled to 10 in wide, 71.4 kg over the STEP's 10,946 cm3. The guard is a 10 mm shell, cast iron at full density; the handwheels cast iron; the lever steel; the dial aluminium

spindle_mass.reason: The spindle nose (solid 2, 839 cm3) in steel, 6.59 kg and 0.0085 kg m2 about its axis, and 0.005 kg m2 for the motor's rotor, which the STEP doesn't draw; the wheel mounted on it adds its own (wheels)

table.reason: Clausing's CSG2A1020 traverses its table 24.41 in by hand, 4.41 in more than its 20 in chuck; the same 4.41 in beyond this 24 in chuck is 28.41 in (721.6 mm), centred on the STEP's pose. At both ends the whole chuck is past the wheel and nothing meets the column or the down-feed handwheel
table.friction_reason: SB1029's table rides ball-bearing slideways: about 0.01 of the table and chuck's 190 kg weight, 19 N

table_handwheel.reason: The larger front handwheel (solids 35-37, 254 mm across), its spinner (36) 117 mm off its axis; positive is clockwise as the operator sees it and drives the table right through its rack, as SB1029's longitudinal handwheel moves the table left and right
table_handwheel.travel_reason: Sharp's SG-618 manual grinder: 2.7 in of table per turn of its longitudinal handwheel. Not self-locking: a push on the table turns the handwheel
table_handwheel.friction_reason: The pinion's bearings and the rack's mesh: a hand turns it with a few newtons at the rim

saddle.reason: Toward the column (+Y) until the table's back edge (y 88.7, solid 41) is 10 mm from the column's face (y 238.7, solid 42); toward the operator 75 mm, past the 61.4 mm that brings the wheel's back face over the chuck's back edge (see gaps)
saddle.friction_reason: Oiled cast-iron ways under the saddle, table, chuck and handwheels, 470 kg at about 0.063

cross_handwheel.reason: The smaller front handwheel (solids 38-40, 200 mm across), its spinner (40) 90.5 mm off its axis; positive is clockwise as the operator sees it, which runs a right-hand screw and the saddle toward the column
cross_handwheel.lead_reason: SB1029 and Clausing CSG2A1020: cross feed 0.2 in per turn of the handwheel, 0.001 in per graduation (200 a turn)
cross_handwheel.friction_reason: The screw's thread and the saddle's ways (0.24 N m of it): 8 N at the rim; self-locking, a 200 N push on the table can't back-drive it (0.16 N m)

wheelhead.reason: Down until the smallest wheel it mounts, the 6 in diamond wheel, has its bottom (z 1273.8 at joint zero) at the chuck's face (z 1059.9, solid 21); the 10 in wheel meets the face 50.8 mm higher, where the operator stops it. Up until the guard's top (z 1500, solid 3) is 5 mm under the column's top (z 1600, solid 42): the 10 in wheel up to 258.1 mm (10.2 in) over the chuck. Lowered for the 6 in wheel, the spindle's housing behind the wheel (from y 38.7, its underside 99 mm under the spindle's axis, solid 3) comes down past the chuck's face: it clears the chuck only while the chuck's back edge is ahead of it (saddle at -10 mm or less), so the work stands within 38 mm of that edge

downfeed_handwheel.reason: The handwheel on the column's right side (solids 43, 45, 46, 200 mm across), its spinner (46) 92.5 mm off its axis; positive is clockwise as the operator at the machine's right sees it, and lowers the wheel
downfeed_handwheel.lead_reason: SB1029: vertical handwheel 0.05 in per turn, 0.0002 in per graduation (250 a turn)
downfeed_handwheel.friction_reason: Self-locking: the head's 30 kg back-drives its screw with only 0.06 N m, so friction holds it; a hand turns it with 10 N at the rim

downfeed_dial.reason: The graduated dial behind the handwheel (solid 44); it turns with the handwheel on its friction, and a hand holding it while the handwheel turns, or turning it alone, sets it to zero
downfeed_dial.friction_reason: A friction-held dial collar: the handwheel carries it (it has 0.001 kg m2 to drag), a fingertip slips it

spindle.reason: The wheel's axis (solids 2, 6, 8), front to back; positive is clockwise as the operator sees it, so the wheel's bottom runs left and throws its sparks left, where SB1029's chip port is (its Figure 1)
spindle.friction_reason: Bearings and windage: the wheel coasts from 3450 rpm to a stop with no brake in about 50 s (the 10 in wheel) or 22 s (the 6 in diamond wheel), as SB1029 asks the operator to let it come to a complete stop

chuck_lever.reason: The lever on the chuck's front (solid 53): its hub at x 267, its ball 317 mm out; it turns in the front plane, positive lifting the ball, from pointing right (the STEP's pose, off) over the top to pointing left (on)
chuck_lever.range_reason: A permanent chuck's handle turns half a turn between off and on (Tormach's chuck: turned to on or off); which end is on isn't in the STEP
chuck_lever.detent_reason: The magnet's pull holds the lever at either end: a torque of 5 N m sin(2 x angle) back toward the nearer end, 16 N at the ball at its worst, 19 N with its 1 N m of friction; past its middle it carries the lever on to its stop (at 8 N m the push it took overloaded the operator's arm, the muscle check over for 18 frames of magnet-on)

spindle.reason: SB1029's and Clausing's spindles run 3450 rpm (a two-pole motor at 60 Hz), as the ct-tpg322 plan takes it: inside the diamond wheel's 6048, and the 6 in diamond wheel then runs 5,420 sfpm
spindle.motor_reason: Between SB1029's 1.5 hp (6 x 18) and Clausing's 3 hp (10 x 20): 4.13 N m at 3450 rpm
spindle.mounted_reason: The diamond wheel (shop.json diamond-wheel-1), the one G2's ct-tpg322 grinds with; the 10 in wheel the STEP draws (gwheel) mounts by its id but isn't started (wheels.gwheel)

guard.reason: OSHA 1910.215(b)(4); the STEP's guard (solids 3, 4) is open below z 1310 between its sides at x +-145 mm: 149.2 deg of the wheel, seen from its axis, starting 15.4 deg below the spindle's horizontal plane; the same for any wheel it holds, its sides being what bounds the opening

chuck.reason: The chuck's top plate (solid 21), 24 x 10 in; Suburban's MCB-1024-FP, 24-1/2 x 10 x 2-5/8 in, is the chuck it stands for (the STEP's is 2.75 in high)
chuck.friction_reason: Ground steel on the chuck's ground face, clean and dry: about 0.2
chuck.rated_reason: McMaster: permanent-magnet chucks hold up to 30 psi (20.7 N/cm2) of a part's face, on thick steel ground flat
chuck.pole_reason: Suburban's fine pole: 1/8 in poles with 1/8 in separators
chuck.thickness_reason: The flux from one pole to the next runs through the part: thinner than a pole's width it saturates, and the hold falls in proportion to its thickness
chuck.gap_reason: The hold falls with the gap g under the part as 1 / (1 + g / 0.3 mm)^2: a 0.1 mm chip or burr costs about 44% of it, which is why SB1029 has both faces ground and cleaned
chuck.reach_reason: Beyond 3 mm the pull is under 1% of its seated value, and it is left out
chuck.working_reason: The flux density that pulls 20.7 N/cm2, B = sqrt(2 mu0 p): below the saturation of steel, so every steel holds alike
chuck.materials_reason: The hold scales with (B / 0.721 T)^2, B the most the part's material can carry: iron and steels, ferritic stainless and cast iron saturate at 1.2-2.15 T, past the chuck's flux, so 1. Carbide's only magnetic phase is its cobalt binder: C2 grade's 6% cobalt by weight is 10.1% by volume (WC 15.63, Co 8.9 g/cm3), 0.183 T of cobalt's 1.81 T, so (0.183 / 0.721)^2 = 0.064. Austenitic stainless, aluminium, brass, bronze and plastics aren't magnetic
chuck.field_reason: The lever's angle a sets the field as (1 - cos a) / 2: none pointing right, all pointing left (proposed)

base.reason: The pedestal (solid 54) above its 50 mm foot; its lower front, 95 mm further out below z 640, is left out

saddle_top.reason: The saddle's top under the table (solid 34)

saddle_arm.reason: The saddle's front arm carrying the handwheels (solid 34)

chuck_face.reason: The chuck's top plate and its poles (solids 21, 9-33): the magnet's face

chuck_lever_hub.reason: The lever's hub and its bend toward the operator (solid 53)

guard_side_left.reason: The guard's left side (solid 3), open below z 1310

housing.reason: The spindle's housing behind the guard, tapering back to the column's slide (solid 3), boxed by its bounds

table_handwheel.reason: The longitudinal handwheel's rim, spokes and hub (solid 37), as a disc

cross_handwheel.reason: The cross-feed handwheel (solid 39), as a disc

downfeed_handwheel.reason: The down-feed handwheel (solid 45), as a disc

controls_box.reason: The control box (made, see gaps): its face toward the operator 75 mm in front of the base, outside the saddle's arm (x 350) and under the table (z 919) through all their travel

chuck_centre.reason: The middle of the chuck's face (solid 21)

wheel_centre.reason: The spindle's axis at the wheel's mid-plane, on the wheelhead so it doesn't turn; the wheel's lowest point (sg_wheel_bottom_head) is made from the mounted wheel

affordances_source.reason: The control box and its buttons aren't in the STEP (see gaps): SB1029's ON button (green, flush) above its OFF button (red, a mushroom pushed in to stop and twisted to reset), with its power light above both, and the optional coolant's switch beside ON. The handwheels' knobs and rims and the lever's ball are the STEP's; which grips work them is the cards'

interlocks: ON runs the wheel only with the OFF button reset (popped out)
pressing OFF stops the wheel's motor and stays in until twisted
the wheel isn't braked: it coasts to a stop
ON doesn't start the spindle on a wheel whose rating isn't confirmed or is under the spindle's speed (SB1029 safety rule 2)
logic.logic_reason: SB1029 Test Run, steps 6-9: OFF is pushed in and twisted clockwise to pop out and reset; with it not reset, ON must not start the machine. Controls: the power light shows the motor running. The chuck is a permanent magnet switched by its lever, with no interlock

coolant.reason: SB1029's optional coolant system (Figure 1, 'Coolant Switch for Optional Coolant System'; Controls, J, the coolant pump switch), fitted by your decision (2026-11-06): its switch on the control box, its nozzle on the guard; the STEP draws neither, so both are made (extract.py), and its tank and pump, under the machine, aren't drawn. The flow is drawn, not simulated: fluids are rendering only, as light and heat are
coolant.switch_reason: A toggle beside ON, as SB1029's panel has it; the pump runs while it is on, whether the wheel runs or not (proposed)
coolant.nozzle_reason: A segmented hose from the guard's front plate (y -51.3, solid 4) down to the grinding point, set for the wheel mounted: its tip 25 mm to the right of the wheel's lowest point, the side the wheel's bottom comes from (it turns clockwise as the operator sees it), 20 mm in front of the wheel's plane and 12 mm above its bottom, aimed at it, so the flow meets the wheel where it enters the cut, and the tip stays clear of the work under it

gwheel.reason: The STEP's wheel (solid 6: 254 mm across, 25.4 wide, a 75 mm bore), its outer flange (8) and blotters (5, 7), as the shop's gwheel (10 x 1 x 3 in, rated 3800 rpm); at a vitrified wheel's 2.2 g/cm3 2.58 kg and 0.0226 kg m2, the steel flange 0.34 kg
gwheel.rating_reason: Not confirmed: gwheel's record gives 3,800 rpm as a 'typical rating', a 7 in wheel's figure; a standard vitrified 10 in wheel is rated 6,500 sfpm, about 2,480 rpm, under the spindle's 3450. So the control won't start the spindle on it until a datasheet gives its rating (the plans agent's check, 2026-11-06)

dwheel-1a1r.reason: Butler Bros' 6 x 0.035 x 1-1/4 in 1A1R resin diamond wheel, 120 grit, 1/4 in of diamond on its rim, 6,048 rpm max; its mid-plane where the 10 in wheel's is [proposed]
dwheel-1a1r.hub_reason: On its own hub between two steel flanges 4 in across and 1/4 in thick, the STEP's flange size, as a thin wheel is clamped: the steel core 0.12 kg, the flanges 0.73
